newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends unchanged as CB sells dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends unchanged as CB sells dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso finished unchanged at 26.37 on Thursday after the Central Bank sold about $33 to $35 million in late trades, dealers said.
The peso initially traded in positive territory when the Central Bank offered six-month reverse repos at a higher-than-market rate of 10.125 percent.
"Many thought interest rates will firm up a little," a foreign bank dealer said. This view gave support to the peso.
However, "the Central Bank started calling around and gave the impression that it wanted to buy dollars," another dealer said.
That spurred banks to buy up the dollar and prodded the Central Bank to eventually sell, he said.
Market volume rose to $159.5 million from $125.0 million the previous day. The volume was still considered light because there were no inflows of arbitrage money, dealers said.
